# Example Output — Azure SWA Custom Domains

*Generated by applying the Azure SWA Custom Domains skill to `example-input.md`.*

---

## 1. DNS record table

| Hostname | Type | Value | TTL | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `www` | CNAME | `<swa-default-hostname>.azurestaticapps.net` | 3600 | already changed — old parking CNAME may still be cached for up to 1 h |
| `@` | A | `<IP from nslookup <swa-default-hostname>.azurestaticapps.net>` | 3600 | replace parking A record; **old 4 h TTL will mask this until ~18:00** |
| `@` | TXT | `<validationToken from az rest>` | 3600 | add for apex validation |
| MX / SPF | — | unchanged | — | not touched |

VentraIP has no ALIAS/ANAME, so the apex uses a static A record. IP documented below with a re-verify note.

## 2. Binding commands

**www — the stalled TLS binding.** Status `Ready` + `sslState: null` + TLS internal-error alert = stalled certificate issuance. Delete and re-add; the re-add validates instantly over the existing CNAME.

```bash
az staticwebapp hostname delete -n stapp-example-prod -g rg-example-prod --hostname www.example.com.au --yes
az staticwebapp hostname set    -n stapp-example-prod -g rg-example-prod --hostname www.example.com.au
# allow up to 15 min, then re-check sslState (section 3)
```

**Apex — TXT validation** (`hostname set` would fail here until DNS settles):

```bash
az rest --method put \
  --uri "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/rg-example-prod/providers/Microsoft.Web/staticSites/stapp-example-prod/customDomains/example.com.au?api-version=2022-09-01" \
  --body '{"properties":{"validationMethod":"dns-txt-token"}}'
# → add returned validationToken as TXT at @ in VentraIP, wait for it at 8.8.8.8, then:
az staticwebapp hostname set -n stapp-example-prod -g rg-example-prod --hostname example.com.au
```

If this returns "CNAME Record is invalid" / not-yet-visible errors: retry every 3 minutes (loop in `reference.md`) — Azure's resolvers are still seeing the parking record.

**Canonicalise apex → www** (once both are Ready):

```bash
az rest --method PUT \
  --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/rg-example-prod/providers/Microsoft.Web/staticSites/stapp-example-prod/customDomains/www.example.com.au?api-version=2024-04-01" \
  --body '{"properties": {"isDefault": true, "validationMethod": "cname-delegation"}}'
```

## 3. TLS / redirect verification

```
$ az staticwebapp hostname list -n stapp-example-prod -g rg-example-prod -o table
Name                  Status   SslState
www.example.com.au    Ready    SniEnabled      ← was null before the re-add
example.com.au        Ready    SniEnabled

$ curl -sI https://www.example.com.au | head -1
HTTP/2 200
$ openssl s_client -servername www.example.com.au -connect www.example.com.au:443 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject
subject=CN = www.example.com.au

$ curl -sI "http://example.com.au/services?utm=x" | grep -i location
location: https://www.example.com.au/services?utm=x       ← 301, path + query preserved
```

If your own machine still shows the parking page or `ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR` after these pass: it is cached DNS from the 4 h parking record — `ipconfig /flushdns` and restart the browser; do not touch the SWA.

## 4. Validation script

`scripts/check-domains.sh` — run after every DNS or hostname change:

```bash
for h in example.com.au www.example.com.au; do
  echo "== $h"; nslookup "$h" 8.8.8.8 | tail -2
  curl -sI "https://$h" | head -1
  openssl s_client -servername "$h" -connect "$h:443" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject
done
curl -sI "http://example.com.au/" | grep -i location    # expect https://www.example.com.au/
```

## 5. Operator notes

- Apex A record IP: `<IP>` (from `nslookup <swa-default-hostname>.azurestaticapps.net`, recorded today). Re-verify if the apex ever stops resolving — Azure may change it.
- Parking A record TTL was 4 h — expect stale client resolution until then; the site was healthy throughout.
- "CNAME Record is invalid" on first attempts was resolver lag, resolved by retry — no DNS was re-edited.
- Wedge watch: if a future `hostname set` goes `RetrievingValidationToken` → `Failed` and its delete sticks in `Deleting`, stop retrying, pull correlation IDs from `az monitor activity-log list --resource-group rg-example-prod --offset 24h`, and plan to serve that hostname from another Azure service — the claim follows the hostname, not the SWA.
